Screened 66 pairs using the Engle-Granger cointegration test (best pair: p = 0.000229).

title: Tham Wai Hong Douglas
text: To test whether a cointegrated pair of SGX listed stocks can generate positive risk-adjusted returns using a pairs trading strategy, and whether a Random Forest model can improve performance.

title: Tham Wai Hong Douglas
text: To test whether a cointegrated pair of SGX listed stocks can generate positive risk-adjusted returns using a pairs trading strategy, and whether a Random Forest model can improve performance.

title: Tham Wai Hong Douglas
text:
Methodlogy

Pulled 5 years of daily price data for 12 SGX-listed stocks using ‘yfinance’.
Screened all 66 pairs for cointegration using Engle-Granger test.
Selected the strongest pair: SingTel(Z74.SI) vs CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (C38U.SI), p = 0.000229.
Calculated the hedge ratio using OLS regression (Beta (β) = 0.2684)
Built a backtesting engine from scrach with a Z-score mean-reversion strategy.
Included transaction cost of 0.1% per trade.
Trained a Random Forest Classifier to predict future spread direction.

title: Tham Wai Hong Douglas
text:
Key Findings







Question
Answer




Q1: Is there a cointegrated pair?
Yes. Singtel vs CapitaLand (p = 0.000229).


Q2: Does the strategy generate positive returns?
Weakly. Sharpe = 0.12, Sortino = 0.048, Max Drawdown = -0.53.


Q3: Can ML improve the strategy?
No. ML Sharpe = -0.26.


Q4: How does it perform across regimes?
Bear = -1.18, Recovery = 0.22, Recent = 0.37.

title: Tham Wai Hong Douglas
text:
Conclusion
The strategy identified a cointegrated pair and generated a small positive return before ML. However, the Sharpe ratio (0.12) and maximum drawdown (-0.53) indicate poor risk-adjusted performance. The Random Forest achieved 52.7% accuracy, which was insufficient to improve strategy. The strategy perform poorly in bear markets and weakly in recovery periods.
